newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end lower ahead of CPI release.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end lower ahead of CPI release.

text.p: Israeli CPI-linked and unlinked bonds closed lower on Thursday a day ahead of the release of January's consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.07 pct to 102.71
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 pct to 101.88.
Volume was low at 116 million shekels.

"CPI-linked bonds closed slightly lower today. These bonds had (previously) made a very big move with yields falling sharply," said Eyal Kolka at Sigma Securities. "I believe that in the long run inflation-linked bonds will continue rising at a slower pace."
CPI-linked long bonds were showing weakness today amid some profit-taking, said Baruch Glicksberg of Clal Insurance.
"Unlinked bonds made a dramatic move during the last few months and yields fell sharply. It's normal to see some profit- taking before the release of the CPI," Kolka added.
The January CPI, due to be published on Friday, is expected to show a rise of about 0.5 percent.
"We saw some overshooting in unlinked bonds on expectations for falling interest rates. These bonds are not expected to continue falling in the near future," Glicksberg said.
Makams, which are also unlinked, closed slightly higher on low volume of only 30 million shekels.

Dollar-linked bonds continued to rise on expectations of a further strengthening of the U.S. currency. In the local forex market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3410 shekels against 3.3420 on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
